name: Philosophy, Politics, and Economics
school: College of Literature, Science, and the Arts

requirements.label: 120 Total Credits
requirements.hint: All credits completed at U-M plus posted transfer credit.

requirements.label: 100 LSA Credits
requirements.hint: Credits from courses recognized by LSA (most U-M courses except some SI offerings and other school-specific courses).

requirements.label: 60 BS-Eligible Credits (for BS students only)
requirements.hint: Only counts for students pursuing a Bachelor of Science.

requirements.label: 90 Credits Excluding Experiential and Independent Study Courses
requirements.hint: At least 90 credits must come from standard coursework; internships and independent study don't count.

requirements.label: 60 Credits outside Philosophy, Politics, and Economics
requirements.hint: Credits earned in courses outside the Philosophy, Politics, and Economics department(s).

requirements.label: 90 Credits of Graded Course Work, Including Transfer and Test
requirements.hint: At least 90 credits must carry a letter grade (transfer and test credit included).

requirements.label: 60 Credits of In-Residence Course Work (AA Campus and U-M Study Abroad)
requirements.hint: Credits taken on the Ann Arbor campus or through an approved U-M study abroad program.

requirements.label: 30 Credits Taken While Enrolled in LSA
requirements.hint: Credits earned while officially enrolled in LSA (as opposed to another U-M college).

requirements.hint: one course required

requirements.label: 100- or 200-Level PHIL Course
requirements.hint: One course, C- or better. Choose 1 of: PHIL 101, PHIL 110, PHIL 196, PHIL 215, PHIL 230, PHIL 263, PHIL 288, PHIL 289, PHIL 297, PHIL 298. Excludes PHIL 180, 183, 201, and 296.

requirements.label: Introductory POLSCI Course
requirements.hint: Choose 1 of: POLSCI 101, 111, 140, or 160. C- or better.

requirements.label: ECON 101 and ECON 102
requirements.hint: Principles of Economics I and II. C- or better.

requirements.label: MATH 115 or Equivalent
requirements.hint: Calculus I or an equivalent, including exam or transfer calculus credit. C- or better.

requirements.label: ECON 401: Intermediate Microeconomic Theory
requirements.hint: C- or better.

requirements.label: PPE 300: Introduction to Political Economy
requirements.hint: C- or better.

requirements.label: PPE 400: Seminar in Political Economy
requirements.hint: C- or better.

requirements.label: Formal Reasoning: Statistics
requirements.hint: One statistics course, C- or better, from the official PPE options: ECON 251, ECON 404, ECON 405, ECON 451, ECON 453, POLSCI 300, STATS 250, STATS 280, or STATS 426. Per the PPE program's Major Requirements page (October 2025) and the LSA bulletin PPE major listing (effective Fall 2025).

requirements.label: Formal Reasoning: Additional Formal Methods Course
requirements.hint: One course in other formal methods central to political economy (statistics, logic, decision theory, or game theory), C- or better, from the official PPE options: ECON 398, ECON 409, PHIL 296, PHIL 303, PHIL 305, PHIL 413, PHIL 414, PHIL 443, PHIL 444, POLSCI 381, POLSCI 391 (also listed as CMPLXSYS 391), POLSCI 488, POLSCI 490, POLSCI 499, or MATH 425 (also listed as STATS 425). Per the PPE program's Major Requirements page (October 2025) and the LSA bulletin PPE major listing (effective Fall 2025); the bulletin also lists SOC 315 for specific 2018 sections only.

requirements.label: Normative Theory: 2 Courses
requirements.hint: Two 300- or 400-level courses in political philosophy, political theory, or welfare economics, C- or better, from the official PPE list: ECON 408/PHIL 408, ECON 496, PHIL 359, 361, 366, 367, 369, 384, 430, 431, 433, 441, 442, 445, 446, POLSCI 301, 302, 306, 400 (appropriate sections), 401 (also WGS 422), 402, 403 (also CLCIV 403), 404, 405, 409, and 495 (appropriate sections). At least one PHIL course must satisfy this requirement or one of the theme courses. Per the LSA bulletin PPE major listing (effective Fall 2025) and the PPE program's Major Requirements page (October 2025).

requirements.label: Political Economy: 2 Courses
requirements.hint: Two courses engaging the economics of government or the politics of economic activity or institutions, C- or better, from the official PPE list: AAS 347/RCSSCI 343/SOC 335, ECON 398, 402, 408 (also PHIL 408), 409, 432, 481, 482, ECON 425/POLSCI 425, POLSCI 322, 337, 340, 341, 343, 348, 363, 364, 369, 387, 389, 391 (also CMPLXSYS 391), 432, 462, 496, and SOC 315. POLSCI 340, 389, and 496 count only in specific titled sections. Per the LSA bulletin PPE major listing (effective Fall 2025) and the PPE program's Major Requirements page (October 2025).

requirements.label: Economics Theme: 3 Courses from a Single Theme
requirements.hint: Still building automatic checking for this rule. Three courses in a single student-designed theme in political economy, C- or better (Honors students take two theme courses plus the Honors thesis sequence). At least two of the courses must be at the 400 level and two must come from distinct academic disciplines; theme courses do not need to come from PHIL, POLSCI, or ECON, and any advanced course from any department that fits the theme may be included once your theme proposal is approved by a PPE advisor. The PPE program posts term-by-term PPE course menus and theme guidance under Major Requirements and Theme Planning. Until then, confirm progress with your advisor.

requirements.label: Departmental Honors: 2 Additional Theme Courses (Honors students only)
requirements.hint: Still building automatic checking for this rule. Two additional advisor approved theme courses for Honors PPE; themes are student designed and may come from any department. Until then, confirm progress with your advisor.

requirements.label: One PHIL Course in Normative Theory or Theme
requirements.hint: At least one PHIL course must be used to satisfy either the normative theory requirement or one of the three theme courses. C- or better.

requirements.label: Major Residence Credits: minimum 16
requirements.hint: Still building automatic checking for this rule. Minimum 16 major credits in residence. The theme portion of the major is student designed with no published list, so this total cannot be counted automatically. Until then, confirm progress with your advisor.

requirements.label: Major Credits: minimum 33
requirements.hint: Still building automatic checking for this rule. Minimum 33 credits from all courses used toward the major, including the student designed theme courses; prerequisites excluded. The theme portion has no published list, so this total cannot be counted automatically. Until then, confirm progress with your advisor.
